title: Are option sellers paid enough for the risk?
summary: Many sellers annualize weekly or monthly premium and assume a high yield. But options are priced on implied volatility, while your P&L depends on realized volatility, what the stock actually does. The real question is whether the premium pays enough for the risk you take.

steps.caption: The stock path drives your actual P&L.
Premium is priced from implied volatility. Annualized, it can look like a large yield.
Realized volatility is what the stock delivers. Here it often runs above implied.
When the gap is zero or negative, the seller is not paid for the risk, whatever the yield looks like.

takeaways: Annualized premium yield does not measure whether you are paid enough.
Options are priced on implied volatility, but P&L follows realized volatility.
Ask whether IV exceeds what the stock is likely to deliver.
